correctness.rationale: For every n>=2, p in (0,1), an explicit transfer matrix yields the exact continuant representation. A pure imaginary root would force consecutive continuants at the same strictly positive parameter to vanish, impossible because f0=f1=1. The positive constant coefficient excludes zero. Degree n-1 is constant, and the fair-coin base point has all roots -1, so all roots remain strictly left of the imaginary axis. Real/conjugate factor grouping gives PGFs on support size at most three. Exact adjacent-transition covariance and the sharp Cauchy variance bound for n-1 Bernoulli factors prove index two is minimal for n>=3 and p!=1/2; n=2 and p=1/2 are explicitly Bernoulli/binomial. Exact-arithmetic diagnostic replay passed 594 coefficient, 396 Hurwitz-minor, and 132 moment comparisons; finite checks are not used to infer the universal claim.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Conditional success-run counts and unconditional two-direction transition counts differ. The conditional real-rootedness statement cannot imply unconditional left-half-plane stability simply by mixing, since mixtures of real-rooted polynomials need not even be stable. For biased length at least three, the unconditional transition law violates the maximum Poisson-binomial variance, so it cannot coincide with the published independent-Bernoulli conditional representation.

value.rationale: A central runs-test statistic has locally dependent indicator representation even for iid observations. The universal left-half-plane zero property supplies a complete independent-factor decomposition with bounded support and the exact factorization index. The strict biased-versus-fair boundary is intrinsic: biased samples of length >=3 are never Poisson-binomial although they always factor into degree-at-most-two PGFs. This is a naturally motivated structural classification across every length and bias, not a computed isolated example.
